shared_elements: shallow incised/low-relief carving on coarse weathered stone
concentric curved or arcing lines used as framing bands
rectangular panels filled with grid/cross-hatched lines
bilaterally symmetrical pairing of two matching motifs side by side
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow, geometric incised relief in which paired symmetrical motifs are enclosed by concentric arcing bands, and both include rectilinear grid- or ladder-filled panels (the twin hatched rectangles in A, the hatched vertical panels on the upper part of B). The decisive difference is the format and the subject: A is a flat slab fragment with a purely abstract, frame-and-centre composition, while B is a freestanding three-dimensional anthropomorphic monolith whose carvings — face, discs, curved chest bands — are organised around a body, so the placement logic and overall impression scarcely correspond.
